preview: Prathamesh Dhole shares his SAP Labs 2022 internship interview experience featuring an online assessment, two technical rounds, and a brief HR round.
content: Interview Experience 2022 SAP Labs Prathamesh Dhole B.Tech IT, 2024 Overview: There were 4 rounds: Online test, Technical round 1, Technical round 2 and HR interview Eligibility criteria: 70% or 7 CGPA and above in current graduating degree and 60% in 10th & 12th Job description: Any (Developer/QA/Support/DevOps/Dev Support) Job location: Bangalore/Pune/Mumbai/Gurgaon Online Assessment (45 minutes) The online assessment was conducted on the SHL platform. It consisted of 2 easy level coding questions. I don’t remember the exact questions but, both the questions were based on array traversal and performing simple calculation. I was able to solve both of them within 10 minutes. Around 40 students were shortlisted for technical round 1 Technical Round 1 (45 minutes) All the interview rounds were conducted in an online mode on Microsoft Teams platform. I thought the interview would start by asking me to introduce myself, but the interviewer began directly with the questions instead. The first question that was asked was a puzzle. Below is the link for the puzzle: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-27-hourglasses-puzzle/ The interviewer asked me to take time to think and tell the approach by showing it in notepad or any other editor. After about 2 minutes I was able to come up with the solution. Then, I was questioned about the differences between flat file systems and databases. Next, he asked me a DSA question. Given an unsorted array of 0s and 1s only determine the count of 0s and 1s in the given array. I answered that we can take two variables count1, count2. count1 would store the count of 0s and count2 would store the count of 1s while traversing the array. Then he asked if we could solve it using a single variable. I replied as the array consists of only 0 and 1, we can simply compute the sum of all elements in the array. This would give us the number of 1s and if we subtract this sum from array length, we would get the number of 0s. He agreed and then moved to the next question. I was not asked to code the solution for this question. After that he asked questions on the OS. What is a deadlock and explain the conditions required for a deadlock to occur. He also asked about the deadlock handling methods. Then, he asked if you were given a large array of integers, compare the various sorting algorithms you know and tell which one you will choose to sort the array. I answered this question by comparing the time complexities of sorting algorithms. Next, he asked the difference between quick sort and merge sort. He then questioned for which data structure merge sort is more preferable and why. At last he asked the different types of SQL commands. (DDL, DML, TCL) 28 students were shortlisted for technical round 2. Technical Round 2 (45 minutes) The interviewer asked me to introduce myself and asked questions such as how is your day till now so as to make me feel comfortable and then started with the questions. The interviewer presented 2-3 code snippets and asked me to identify errors within them. There were some syntactical errors. I was able to answer correctly and he also seemed satisfied. Then, he asked a DSA question. Given a linked list and a specific number 'k', I was asked to determine the count of occurrences of the number 'k' within the linked list. He first asked me to tell the approach and then, share screen and code it in any editor of my choice. After that, I was questioned about the four pillars of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP). Then, I was asked to define polymorphism and explain the difference between runtime polymorphism and compile-time polymorphism. Next, he also asked what inheritance is. Which are the types of inheritances in JAVA. Which type of inheritance is not possible in JAVA? Then, I was questioned about exception handling in JAVA. I explained what exception handling is with the help of an example and how it helps to manage errors in code. After that I was asked about normalization in DBMS. I explained the concept of normalization and why it is required. He then asked about my interests in technology. I shared my personal interests and opinions related to technological advancements. Then, a puzzle was asked. You're standing on the surface of Earth. You walk 1 km south, 1 km west, and 1 km north. You end up exactly where you started. Where are you? The answer is the North Pole. The interviewer was happy as I quickly answered this question. Also, in this round the interviewer asked me to explain my projects. If you worked on group projects, explain your role in that project and be clear with the technologies you used. At the end of the interview, the interviewer asked me if I had any questions or not. I asked him about the team he was working with and his experience with SAP till now. 9 students were shortlisted for the HR Round HR Round (5 minutes) At the beginning only, the HR mentioned that it is going to be a quick call. She first asked me to introduce myself and then asked about the preferred locations. Atlast, she asked if I had any questions. Whenever the interviewer asks you for questions don’t say no. Keep some questions ready beforehand by doing research about the company. All the 9 students who appeared for the HR round were selected for the summer internship. After reading the interview experience you must have got that the overall difficulty of the interview was easy. Just the thing is you need to be prepared with everything, from DSA to CS fundamentals to puzzles. Stick to limited resources and prepare accordingly. Resources Followed: 1. DSA: GeeksForGeeks, Striver's SDE Sheet, takeUforward (For recursion, backtracking, graphs, trees and dynamic programming) 2. OS: Gate Smashers OS Playlist, GFG OS Notes 3. DBMS: Gate Smashers DBMS Playlist, GFG DBMS Notes 4. OOPS: Javatpoint, GeeksForGeeks 5. Puzzles: For puzzles I did not refer to any specific website. You can refer to GeeksForGeeks which has a number of puzzles. Tips: 1. Prepare your introduction well. Keep it simple and short. 2. Do not lie on your resume. Have complete understanding of all the technologies you mentioned in the resume. 3. Research well about a company before applying. Go through the interview experiences of your seniors. 4. Think out loud and let the interviewer know your thought process. They help you to be on the right path. 5. Don't get demotivated if you don't get selected in a company. Learn from the mistakes you made, keep studying and prepare for the next opportunity.
